$comment: The shared fixtures. Both the TypeScript suite and the Swift suite decode every file listed here; a drift on either side fails the build. `envelope: "ok"` means the file is a full success envelope and `schema` names the type of its `data`. `envelope: "raw"` means the file IS the named schema.

fixtures.summary: A deferral must always return a strictly later instant. This is the guarantee refusing to be broken.
A valid token that is not for this surface. The only place Syl tells a caller apart from an unauthenticated one, and it is safe because they already hold a working credential.
Every write takes a key. Absence is an error, not a default.
Same key, different body. The outbox must not silently write twice.
Retryable, and deliberately says nothing about internals.
404. The code is the contract; the status is advisory.
The one refusal that means stop retyping and go get another code. Only a caller holding the right code can see it.
Ten minutes passed, or another code superseded this one. Distinguishable from a wrong guess only to someone who knows the code.
Quiet hours gate speaking, not working.
Retryable, with a server-suggested backoff floor.
Never retried. Retrying an auth failure fifty times is the worst possible response.
The Mac is up but a dependency is not. Retryable.
VALIDATION_FAILED carries { field, reason }[] in details.
A paired device's bearer token.
There is exactly one principal.
The Commander's own durable thread, at the well-known id.
The interactive lane plus one job lane.
The outbox view: sent, retried, and never acknowledged.
The only state that satisfies the guarantee: ackedAt is set, by the device.
One notification for a batch deferred past quiet hours. deliveredAt set, ackedAt still null.
APNs refused. The row survives, attempts climb, nextAttemptAt is set — nothing is dropped.
A TestFlight build: production token. The full token is never returned.
Both environments at once — which is why routing is per token, not global.
Goals self-nest; the horizon is derived from targetDate, not stored.
Includes a dormant goal — a real state, not a soft delete.
Reachable, but APNs is failing. Reminders still queue. `build` is null and turnsInFlight absent: this one was started from source by hand, which is a real state and not a missing field.
Everything up, and saying which commit is answering. A stale build passes every other check on this page, so `build` is the only field that can catch it.
maxTurns: 0. A job that cannot spawn a turn cannot be delayed by a rate limit or broken by a model declining to act.
Resumable, leased, background. The lease is what makes reboot recovery possible.
Backs the admin's 'Next' view.
The HTTP half of optimistic-send reconciliation. `seq` here is the MESSAGE sequence.
History, newest first, mid-pagination.
A one-shot commitment. Fires late rather than vanishing.
Pushed out of quiet hours. deferredFrom keeps the chain visible; nextFireAt is strictly later.
Recurring; supersedesPrevious, so yesterday's does not pile up.
A page of reminders across states.
Ran 6 minutes late after a reboot. latenessMs is the metric that says whether the trigger design works.
Hit a budget ceiling. Suspended and asking — not killed silently.
Reminder delivery: zero turns, zero cost, no summary. Lateness recorded regardless.
Backs the admin's 'Ran' and 'Failed' views.
A device back from a week away pages: hasMore is true.
Cursor sync — the device's 'pull since cursor' step. Not the WebSocket sync frame.
An explicit ask. Never provisional.
Inferred structure — provisional, visible, expires if unresolved.
Includes the delegatedJobId seam between the life model and the job system.
The only thing that marks a reminder delivered.
`why` is the only optional field Syl should ever push for.
The RRULE subset is deliberate; anything outside it is rejected, not half-supported.
Wall time plus IANA zone. Never a fixed offset.
An explicit ask lands as open, never proposed.
Exchanged once per device for a bearer token.
environment travels with the token, because both exist at once during development.
clientId is required — without it an optimistic send cannot be reconciled.
Exactly one of until or minutes. The result must be strictly later.
Server speaks first. A client that sends auth_response unprompted is closed on.
Auth is a frame, not a header — the browser WebSocket API cannot set one.
clientId reconciles the optimistic bubble; idempotencyKey stops a retry becoming a second message.
lastSeq is the FRAME sequence, not a message sequence.
Carries BOTH sequences: seq is the frame stream, messageSeq is the conversation.
fatal:true means stop reconnecting and re-pair, rather than loop against a wall.
fatal:false is informational; the socket stays up.
Application-level, above any transport ping.
Echoes the client ts and adds the server's own clock.
The default. During quiet hours it is absent unconditionally.
Couples 1:1 to a time-sensitive reminder. If it is not worth breaking through Focus, it is not worth alert.
The frame quoted verbatim in the character proposal.
A turn is in flight. No seq — never replayed.
Numbered and replayable. `seq` is the frame stream; `message.seq` is the conversation.
complete:false — the gap aged out of the buffer. The client must fall back to GET /sync, not assume it is caught up.
The gap, replayed. frames never contains a presence frame.
sinceSeq, NOT since. Conflating it with the HTTP cursor is the bug this naming prevents.
